newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures steady, but outperform other markets.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures steady, but outperform other markets.

text.p: Bunds futures were nearly unchanged in late trade, but outperformed other bond markets on the day as the strong mark made German investments more attractive.
Analysts said they see the market taking a breather after recent strong gains, likely trading between the December contract high of 100.47 and important psychological support at 100.00.
The DTB December contract stood in the middle of that range at 100.32 in late trade, down two basis points on the day.
"The market is taking a breather. We are due to consolidate for the time being," said Ian Ford, bond market analyst at MCM YieldWatch in London.

Analysts said German unemployment numbers, slightly worse than expected, gave Bunds a short-lived boost. Seasonally adjusted unemployment rose 41,000. The figures, they said, had added weight after German manufacturing data earlier in the week also pointed to slow economic growth.
Bunds did well against other European markets and Treasuries. The T-note/bund gap widened to 52 basis points from 46 basis points, helped by strong mark.
Bunds had been lower much of the day after tracking Treasuries down after a Japanese finance ministry official said the dollar's recovery from a slide last year was about to finish.
Analysts said the yield curve steepened on the day due to demand for two-year notes. The demand, they said, was due to a technical rebound after recent declines in short maturities.
But Ford at MCM said the steeping curve was unlikely to last and that the yield curve's recent flattening trend was likely to resume. --Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 756525
